channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Apesar do apoio nacional, PDT vai enfrentar o PT em Minas com Kalil
item.description: Despite the national alliance between PDT and PT, in Minas Gerais the parties will maintain separate candidacies for the state government. The PDT supports Alexandre Kalil’s pre-candidacy, who appears in second place in polls with 14%, while the PT officially nominated Patrus Ananias, who has not yet appeared in polls. The PDT’s state leadership argues that Kalil has stronger electoral performance and that backing Patrus would mean abandoning a competitive position.

item.title: Crusoé: “Green Card quem precisa é o produtor brasileiro”, diz Caiado
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized former deputy Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL) for receiving a U.S. green card, arguing that what Brazil needs is access to the American market for its producers — without having to pay extra costs or face barriers.

item.title: Sargento preso por morte de capitã já atuou na segurança de Zema
item.description: Sergeant Eduardo Abner Pereira de Oliveira, suspected of killing Captain Michele Leão Azevedo of the PMMG, was arrested after bringing her body to the hospital, claiming she fell down the stairs. He previously worked in the security detail for Governor Romeu Zema and was removed from ASPRA/PMBM due to disciplinary issues. The Civil Police are investigating the case as homicide, with evidence of bodily injuries and ecstasy use.

item.title: Entenda a proposta do setor de máquinas para conter impacto do tarifaço
item.description: Abimaq presented to the Lula government a package of measures to mitigate the effects of the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian products, including the reinstatement of Reintegra, pre-export credit lines, federal tax deferrals, expanded ApexBrasil actions, and adjustments to the Brazil Soberano program. The proposals aim to reduce the 'Brazil cost,' increase competitiveness, and diversify export markets.

item.title: Brasil tem 918,9 mil eleitores no exterior; veja onde eles estão
item.description: The number of Brazilian voters abroad eligible to vote in the 2026 elections reached 918,900, a 31.8% increase over four years. The largest voting posts are in Lisbon (Portugal), Boston (USA), and Porto (Portugal), with the U.S. having the highest number of eligible voters (265,000), followed by Portugal (134,000) and Japan (88,300). Despite this historical growth, abstention among overseas voters remains high, with 51% not voting in past elections.

item.title: PL adia convenção em Minas e cogita realizar encontro sem definir candidato ao governo, prolongando o impasse de Flávio no estado
item.description: The PL postponed its Minas Gerais convention to July 27 without yet defining a gubernatorial candidate, prioritizing efforts to persuade Senator Cleitinho (Republicanos) to run for governor. The decision considers Cleitinho’s personal mourning after his brother’s death and his current unwillingness to engage in politics, with the party considering approving only proportional candidacies at the convention and delaying the majoritarian ticket until the August 5 deadline. This uncertainty complicates Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential campaign, as Minas Gerais is the country’s second-largest electoral college.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Trump “perdeu um pouco o rumo” ao taxar Brasil
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL party, criticized Donald Trump's decision to include Brazil in the U.S. tariff package, calling it 'madness' and stating that Trump 'lost his way'. He advocated for diplomatic negotiation to reverse the tariffs, citing Flávio Bolsonaro's recent U.S. visit as evidence of inconsistent U.S. policy.

item.title: Zema nega convite para Michelle Bolsonaro ser vice após atrito gerado com a cúpula do PL
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo) denied having made any formal invitation to Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) to be his running mate in 2026, stating he only mentioned her name as a possibility in response to a journalist's question. Michelle had already publicly ruled out the idea, noting she has not yet decided whether to run for Senate and that, as a PL member, she cannot run on a separate ticket from her party, which has already nominated Flávio Bolsonaro as its presidential candidate. Zema’s comment provoked irritation within the PL leadership, which viewed it as an attempt to exploit internal divisions within the Bolsonarist movement to boost his own candidacy.

item.title: Nova pesquisa mostra disputa voto a voto entre Lula e Flávio na região mais populosa do país
item.description: The Real Time Big Data poll shows Lula leading in the Northeast with 54% voting intentions, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads in the South with 41%. In the Southeast, the country's most populous region, both candidates are tied at 37%, indicating a vote-by-vote race. Other candidates like Renan Santos (12%) and Ronaldo Caiado (7%) also show strong performance in the Southeast.

item.title: Candidatos à Presidência poderão gastar até R$ 133,4 milhões na campanha de 2026, decide TSE
item.description: The TSE has set the campaign spending limit for the 2026 presidential race at R$133.4 million, as officially published in a regulation on Tuesday (21). The cap applies to all candidates running for President of the Republic in the October 2026 elections.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro reforça queixa-crime contra Janones no STF
item.description: The defense of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro filed a supplement to a criminal complaint against federal deputy André Janones at the Supreme Court, claiming Janones' recent statements confirm a 'deliberate and illicit strategy' of insults, including calling Bolsonaro a 'bandit', 'thief', and 'militiaman'. Janones said he will continue using such terms and declared his goal is the 'annihilation and complete extermination of Bolsonarism'. The defense argues the remarks exceed free speech protections and are not legitimate political criticism.

item.title: O plano de governo de Renan Santos
item.description: The Mission Party, founded by the Free Brazil Movement (MBL), unveiled a government plan for Renan Santos’ pre-candidacy to the Presidency, proposing a deep reform of the Brazilian state, including cutting approximately 70% of the country’s municipalities. The text only describes the plan’s content, without further details on other proposals or political context.

item.title: Bolsonaro é quem decidirá vice de Flávio, diz presidente do PL
item.description: PL party president Valdemar Costa Neto stated that former President Jair Bolsonaro will decide the vice-presidential candidate on the ticket of his eldest son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), for the 2026 elections. The comment was made in a Reuters interview on Tuesday, underscoring Bolsonaro’s central role in shaping the party’s electoral strategy.

item.title: Oposição resgata fala de 2021 em que Lula compara Ortega a Merkel
item.description: Brazilian opposition revived a 2021 video in which Lula compares Daniel Ortega's prolonged rule in Nicaragua to that of leaders like Angela Merkel and Felipe González, advocating for power alternation while stating he cannot interfere in other nations' sovereign decisions. He added that if Ortega imprisoned opposition figures to prevent electoral competition, such action would be 'totally wrong'.

item.title: PF encerra processo e decide demitir Eduardo Bolsonaro por abandono de cargo
item.description: The Federal Police concluded the administrative disciplinary process against Eduardo Bolsonaro and decided on his dismissal for abandonment of duty. The former deputy has lived in the U.S. since February 2025 as a political exile, having lost his mandate in December 2024 due to unjustified absences. He was sentenced by the STF to four years and two months in prison for coercion against the Judiciary.

item.title: Real Time Big Data: candidato mais competitivo contra Lula no 2º turno não é Flávio
item.description: According to the Real Time Big Data survey, former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) is the only adversary of Lula who numerically leads in the second-round simulation, with 44% versus Lula’s 43%, though within the margin of error, resulting in a technical tie. Caiado demonstrates the highest competitiveness among tested opponents, outperforming Flávio Bolsonaro, Renan Santos and others, despite having only 7% in the first round. Other scenarios show Lula ahead, but the Caiado matchup is the most competitive.

item.title: Acordo com Tereza Cristina (PP) para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro não avançou, afirma Valdemar
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto stated that no agreement could be reached for Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) to be the vice-presidential candidate on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) ticket for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Áudio: 158 milhões de brasileiros podem votar nas eleições de outubro
item.description: Over 158 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in the 2026 elections, an increase of 2.2 million compared to the previous election. Women make up nearly 53% of the electorate, and approximately 3.5 million voters are 18 years old or younger. São Paulo, Minas Gerais, and Rio de Janeiro concentrate the largest electoral colleges in the country.

item.title: Trump perdeu o rumo com tarifaço contra o Brasil, diz presidente do PL
item.description: PL party leader Valdemar Costa Neto criticized Donald Trump for imposing 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, stating that Trump 'lost his way' and that the move harms the long-standing trade partnership between the U.S. and Brazil. He emphasized that Brazil has always been a key U.S. partner and that the tariffs hurt both American and Brazilian interests. The tariffs were announced one day after Flávio Bolsonaro’s visit to the U.S., which Valdemar described as 'madness'.

item.title: Lula defende soberania na véspera de tarifaço: "Brasil não se entrega"
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defended national sovereignty in a social media post one day before the U.S. imposed 25% tariffs on Brazilian goods, declaring 'Brazil will not surrender'. The tariffs, affecting approximately $7.4 billion in Brazilian exports to the U.S., were based on a USTR investigation under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, alleging unfair Brazilian trade practices. Despite the tariffs, the U.S. granted exceptions for essential goods such as coffee, beef and rare earths, while the Lula government prepares relief measures for impacted industries.

item.title: TSE: teto para campanha presidencial pode chegar a R$ 133,5 milhões
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) released the spending limits for the 2026 elections, adjusted for inflation based on the IPCA. Presidential candidates may spend up to R$ 88.9 million in the first round and an additional R$ 44.5 million in a potential runoff, totaling a ceiling of R$ 133.5 million. The adjustment reflects inflation correction to ensure fairness in electoral contests.

item.title: Sem aliança, Flávio chega a convenção sob crítica do centrão de favorecimento à família e inabilidade
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro arrives at the PL convention to formalize his 2026 presidential bid without support from the centrão, facing criticism for poor dialogue and lack of political strategy. Once seen as the most politically adept Bolsonaro family member, he is now accused of favoring family interests and demonstrating an inability to build the alliances needed for a competitive campaign.

item.title: LULA ameaça VIDA de FLÁVIO de NOVO, enquanto isso, FLÁVIO SEGUE CRESCENDO nas PESQUISAS
item.description: Former President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva allegedly threatened the life of former Rio de Janeiro governor Flávio Bolsonaro, according to social media reports. Despite the accusations, Flávio Bolsonaro continues to show growth in voter intention polls for the 2026 elections. The content reflects an escalating political tension between government allies and opposition figures.

item.title: Zema propõe tirar controle da Petrobras do governo e transformar a estatal em 'corporation'
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for the Novo party, proposed turning Petrobras into a 'corporation' where the government remains a shareholder without managerial control, advocating full privatization of the energy sector to boost efficiency and end political interference in state enterprises. He also denied having offered the vice-presidential spot to Michelle Bolsonaro, stating her name was only raised by a journalist and that no invitation was ever made.

item.title: Candidatos à Presidência poderão gastar R$ 133 mi em caso de 2º turno
item.description: On July 21, 2026, the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) released spending limits for the 2026 elections, maintaining the same amounts as in 2022. Presidential candidates may spend up to R$ 88.9 million in the first round and an additional R$ 44.4 million in a potential runoff, totaling R$ 133.3 million. For state offices, such as governor in São Paulo, the limit is R$ 26.6 million in the first round and R$ 13.3 million in the second, while federal and state deputies have fixed ceilings of R$ 3.1 million and R$ 1.2 million, respectively.

item.title: O salto de Renan Santos na nova pesquisa Real Time Big Data
item.description: Renan Santos emerges as the main alternative outside the polarization between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), with 9% voting intentions in the Real Time Big Data poll, up from 6% on June 1. His strongest support comes from high-income voters (15%), youth aged 16–34 (12%), and the Southeast region (12%), with 55% loyalty among supporters. In a simulated runoff against Lula, the president would win 44% to 35%.

item.title: Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro: a eleição do desalento
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election is marked by voter disillusionment, with few citizens enthusiastic about the available options. Lula seeks a fourth term without the hope of 2002 or the emotional drive of 2022, while Flávio Bolsonaro has lost his appeal as a 'moderate Bolsonaro,' now seen as equally radical as his father by most voters. Alternative candidates such as Caiado, Zema, and Renan Santos fail to gain significant traction, remaining far below 10% in voting intention.

item.title: O novo homem-bomba para a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Close allies of Flávio Bolsonaro have begun monitoring Thiago Miranda, a publicist linked to Daniel Vorcaro and targeted in the 10th phase of Operation Compliance Zero. The move suggests a potential campaign strategy involving controversial figures tied to financial fraud schemes.

item.title: Repositório reúne decisões do TSE sobre desinformação eleitoral
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has launched the Electoral Disinformation Decisions Repository (R eade), a public tool that compiles rulings on the removal or retention of misleading content threatening electoral integrity. Available on the TSE portal, the repository complies with Resolution No. 23.732/2024, enhancing transparency and public access to electoral jurisprudence on disinformation.

item.title: Aécio: PSDB vai priorizar bancada no Congresso para liderar projeto presidencial em 2030
item.description: The PSDB, led by Aécio Neves, has decided not to run a presidential candidate in 2026, instead focusing on electing 35 federal deputies and state-level candidates to rebuild its base and launch a presidential project by 2030, amid Brazil's deep polarization between Lulism and Bolsonarism.

item.title: Brasil ‘pode desempenhar papel sério em esforços de paz’, diz porta-voz da Ucrânia
item.description: The spokesperson for Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Heorhii Tykhyi, stated that Brazil could play a serious role in peace efforts regarding the war against Russia, citing Lula’s dialogue with Putin and Brazil’s repeated calls for a ceasefire. He praised the recent meeting between Lula and Zelensky in France and reiterated an open invitation for Brazilian officials, including Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, to visit Ukraine. The Brazilian government has previously affirmed its support for a negotiated solution, with UN mediation and direct engagement between the parties.

item.title: Lula é aprovado por 49% e desaprovado por 48%, diz Indexa
item.description: The Indexa Pesquisas survey shows President Lula's approval at 49%, slightly above disapproval at 48%, with 3% undecided. Although approval is technically tied, negative evaluations of the government (41%) exceed positive ones (33%). On re-election, 51% of Brazilians oppose a new term for Lula, while only 36% support it, indicating that support for continuity is more restricted than current government approval.

item.title: Deltan Dallagnol aciona a Justiça para obter ‘selo’ de elegível
item.description: Former deputy Deltan Dallagnol filed a request with the TRE-PR for a preemptive declaration of eligibility for the 2026 elections, arguing that his 2023 TSE cassation did not declare him ineligible or establish an eight-year ban. His defense claims recent STF rulings on content disclosure have created a 'reasonable doubt' about his electoral status, justifying early review. Dallagnol seeks legal certainty before formalizing his Senate candidacy in Paraná.

item.title: PF conclui processo e recomenda demissão de Eduardo Bolsonaro por abandono de cargo; decisão cabe ao ministro da Justiça
item.description: The Federal Police concluded an administrative disciplinary proceeding against Eduardo Bolsonaro for abandonment of duty following his move to the United States in 2025 and recommended his dismissal as a police clerk. The final decision rests with Justice Minister Wellington Lima e Silva. Bolsonaro was removed from the Chamber of Deputies in December 2025 due to excessive absences and unanimously convicted by the STF in June 2026 for obstruction of justice.

item.title: Quanto candidatos a presidente poderão gastar na campanha de 2026, segundo o TSE
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has set campaign spending limits for the 2026 elections, maintaining the same values as in 2022. Presidential candidates may spend up to R$ 88.9 million in the first round and R$ 44.4 million in a potential runoff. For other offices, limits vary: R$ 26.6 million for São Paulo governor in the first round, R$ 7.1 million for São Paulo senator, R$ 3.1 million for federal deputy, and R$ 1.2 million for state deputy, with a fine of 100% of the excess amount for those who exceed the ceiling.

item.title: Lula e Flávio têm fragilidades expostas na campanha
item.description: The formation of party tickets during the 2026 conventions generated media attention due to unresolved alliances, but these are not the core issues affecting the candidacies of Lula and Flávio. The article suggests deeper, unspecified fragilities are being exposed in the campaign. The focus is on identifying what truly weakens the candidacies beyond surface-level alliance disputes.

item.title: Governo estuda crédito e novos mercados contra tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Lula government is studying expanded credit lines, adjustments to the Brazil Sovereign Plan, and new market access to counter the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian goods, effective July 22, 2026. Industrial groups like Abimaq advocate reducing the 'Brazil cost' and broadening eligibility in the Brazil Sovereign Plan to boost competitiveness.

item.title: O lamento de Flávio por se ver distante da ‘vice ideal’
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro prefers economist Daniella Marques as his 2026 vice-presidential running mate due to her combative profile and financial market ties, despite her party, Republicanos, being neutral and the deadline for party changes having passed. He views agribusiness support as already secured with Teresa Cristina, making her inclusion less urgent.

item.title: Nova pesquisa Datafolha para presidente será divulgada na sexta-feira (24)
item.description: Folha de S.Paulo will release a new Datafolha poll on Friday (24) showing voting intentions for president and approval of Lula’s (PT) government. The survey comes amid ongoing debates about the current administration and prospects for the 2026 elections.

item.title: PF deve encerrar inquérito do Master em um mês
item.description: The Federal Police is expected to conclude its investigation into banking fraud at Banco Master by the end of August, with Daniel Vorcaro almost certain to be indicted and politicians like Jaques Wagner set to testify on August 7. Concurrently, 2026 election preparations are underway as parties finalize candidacies and the PF investigates alleged use of parliamentary amendments for political influence. Polls show two-thirds of Flávio Bolsonaro’s voters may switch to defeat Lula, with Ronaldo Caiado seen as a useful vote and Lula in a technical tie with Flávio and Caiado in a potential runoff.

item.title: Crusoé: Biden brasileiro tem medo de debate
item.description: Lula's campaign is considering avoiding debates and sabatinas before the 2026 first round to protect his image, amid criticism from Flávio Bolsonaro, a PL pré-candidate, who dubbed him the 'Brazilian Biden'. The move aims to mitigate reputational risks ahead of the election.

item.title: Presidente do MDB responde ao STF e nega participação na indicação de emendas
item.description: The national president of the MDB, federal deputy Baleia Rossi (SP), sent responses to Justice Flávio Dino of the STF denying that the party’s presidency participates in the indication of parliamentary amendments. He emphasized that amendment decisions are the individual prerogative of each legislator. The statement was made in response to the minister’s inquiries about potential irregularities in resource allocation.

item.title: Dívidas com agências reguladoras disparam, e balcão único de negociação fracassa
item.description: Debts owed by individuals and companies to regulatory agencies surged in 2026, while the Lula government's plan to create a single negotiation desk to speed up payments and boost revenue failed. The main reason for the failure was the lack of consensus among stakeholders on establishing a new agency responsible for collection, which prevented the implementation of the proposed model.

item.title: Como se nada estivesse a acontecer
item.description: The article criticizes the absence of ecological crisis debate in Brazil's 2026 elections, despite escalating environmental devastation and global climate impacts. Hegemonic left sectors remain trapped in developmentalist nostalgia, while fear of Bolsonaro's return dominates the agenda, ignoring urgent issues like floods, wildfires, and climate migration. The author warns that Brazil is choosing between submission to U.S. imperialism and neglect of its own ecological survival.

item.title: André do Prado posta foto ao lado de Tarcísio, Flávio e Derrite
item.description: André do Prado (PL), president of the Alesp, posted a photo alongside Tarcísio de Freitas, Flávio Bolsonaro, and Guilherme Derrite, reinforcing their alliance for the 2026 Senate race, with Prado taking the slot originally meant for Eduardo Bolsonaro, who remains first alternate despite his STF conviction.

item.title: Meio-Dia em Brasília: Eduardo Bolsonaro é norte-americano; Caiado desafia Lula
item.description: A new electoral poll shows Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) numerically ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a potential 2026 runoff. The program also notes Eduardo Bolsonaro holds U.S. citizenship, raising eligibility concerns, and highlights the PT's apprehension about upcoming debates and candidate interrogations.

item.title: Governo Lula minimiza alianças restritas à esquerda e celebra Centrão neutro
item.description: Lula's allies downplay the fact that his presidential alliances are limited to left-wing parties, emphasizing that many members of the Centrão are expected to openly support his re-election. They view the likely neutrality of center-party blocs as a greater victory for Lula than for Flávio Bolsonaro, who struggles to build a coalition without notable progress. The Centrão’s neutrality is seen as strategically advantageous for the Workers’ Party campaign.

item.title: A 4 dias de convenção, Flávio Bolsonaro não tem vice nem partidos na chapa
item.description: Four days before the PL's national convention, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has yet to define a vice-presidential running mate or solidify party alliances for the presidential race. Resistance from Centrão parties, particularly the União Brasil-PP federation—which is expected to declare neutrality—and the Republicans, which favors not supporting national candidates, hinders coalition-building. The uncertainty reduces Bolsonaro’s projected radio and TV ad time to about four minutes per block, compared to Lula’s slightly over five minutes.

item.title: Tarifaço: setor de máquinas diz não apoiar reciprocidade e defende ampliação de programa de crédito para empresas afetadas
item.description: The Brazilian Machinery and Equipment Industry Association (Abimaq) opposed the proposed tariff reciprocity by the Lula government in response to U.S. tariffs, advocating for diplomatic and business channels instead. The group urged expansion of the Brazil Soberano credit program to support affected firms, alongside strengthening international negotiations and diversifying markets. Abimaq President José Velloso noted that despite U.S. trade barriers, the sector’s exports rose 12% over the past year, reaching a record high.

item.title: Crusoé: Renan Santos alcança a barreira dos 10%
item.description: Renan Santos, candidate of the Missão party, reached 9% in voting intentions in the Realtime Big Data poll released on April 21, marking his best performance so far and placing him third. Lula leads with 40%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro in second. The poll was published by Crusoé and referenced by O Antagonista.
